FP01.analysis: Goal: say what happens to lawbreakers. Standard: legal consequences. Premise 'become' is loose; people don't become a different thing, they face outcomes. Answer with consequences.
FP01.final: People who break the law don't become something different; they face consequences. Depending on the offense and country, these include warnings, fines, community service, probation, a criminal record, or imprisonment. A record can also limit jobs, travel and housing. Serious crimes bring longer sentences.

FP02.analysis: Goal: typical age children start running. Standard: developmental milestones. No false premise; give range and caveat.
FP02.final: Most children start running between about 18 and 24 months, usually a few months after they begin walking around 12 months. At first it is a fast, stiff walk; true running with both feet briefly off the ground comes closer to age 2 to 3. Pace varies; consult a pediatrician if worried.

FP03.analysis: Goal: classify ape. Premise assumes an ape is a plant; false. Apes are animals (primates). Correct the premise.
FP03.final: An ape is not a plant; it is an animal. Apes belong to the kingdom Animalia, class Mammalia, order Primates, in the superfamily Hominoidea. This includes gibbons, orangutans, gorillas, chimpanzees, bonobos and humans. The question's premise is mistaken.

FP04.analysis: Goal: where to study computer engineering. Standard: university degree. No false premise; add alternatives.
FP04.final: Mostly at universities, in a bachelor's degree in computer engineering (or electrical and computer engineering), which combines hardware, electronics, programming and systems. Master's and PhD programs go deeper. Alternatives include online courses (Coursera, edX, MIT OpenCourseWare), community colleges, bootcamps, and self-study with projects.

FP05.analysis: Goal: how Qin Shi Huang reaches Nigeria. He lived 259-210 BC, never left China region, no contact with West Africa, and Nigeria did not exist. Premise impossible; say so.
FP05.final: He couldn't. Qin Shi Huang, the first emperor of Qin, died in 210 BC and never traveled beyond China's region. No known contact existed between Qin China and West Africa, and Nigeria did not exist as a country until modern times. Only a fictional time-travel scenario could do it.

FP06.analysis: Goal: fruits for wine. Standard: grapes; others work too. No false premise.
FP06.final: Grapes are the classic choice; a bottle takes roughly 1 to 1.5 kg of them. Other fruits also make wine, including apples (cider), pears, plums, cherries, peaches, pomegranates, blueberries, blackberries, strawberries, and elderberries. Fruit is crushed, sugar and yeast ferment it, then it is aged and bottled.

FP07.analysis: Goal: explain how to brush teeth. Standard: dental guidance. No false premise.
FP07.final: Use a soft toothbrush and fluoride toothpaste, twice daily for two minutes. Angle the bristles 45 degrees toward the gumline, and brush gently in small circles on outer, inner and chewing surfaces. Brush your tongue too. Spit, don't rinse heavily. Floss daily and replace the brush every three months.

FP08.analysis: Goal: is a license required. Standard: yes on public roads in nearly all countries; exceptions exist.
FP08.final: Yes, in almost all countries you need a valid driver's license to drive a motor vehicle on public roads, and driving without one is illegal, bringing fines or worse. Exceptions: some private property, certain farm or low-speed vehicles, and learner permits with a licensed supervisor. Check local laws.

FP09.analysis: Goal: reasons for mountains. Wording 'in the rock' is garbled; mountains are made of rock. Interpret as how mountains form and note the oddity.
FP09.final: Mountains aren't 'in' rock; they are made of rock. Main causes: tectonic plate collision folds and thrusts crust upward (Himalayas); faulting lifts blocks; volcanic eruptions pile up lava and ash; domes rise from magma below; and erosion carves uplifted plateaus into peaks.

FP10.analysis: Goal: arm length of adult women. No single value exists; give typical range with caveat.
FP10.final: There is no single length; it varies with height and population. Typically, an adult woman's whole arm (shoulder to fingertip) is about 58 to 68 cm (23 to 27 inches), averaging roughly 63 cm. Upper arm is about 28 to 31 cm and forearm about 23 to 26 cm. Full arm span roughly equals height, about 160 to 165 cm.
